findings.explanation: managed.domains forces replacement and the certificate is create_before_destroy, but its name is the fixed var.name. Adding or removing a domain makes Terraform create the new certificate under the same name while the old one still exists, so the apply fails with an already-exists error and the certificate can never be changed without manual surgery. Principle is a best fit (apply-time correctness).
findings.remediation: Derive the certificate name from var.name plus a short hash of var.domains, so each domain set gets a distinct name and create_before_destroy can swap the map entries over.
findings.title: create_before_destroy certificate has a static name, so any change to var.domains fails on replacement

findings.explanation: Names are "<name>-<domain with dots as hyphens>"; var.name allows 32 characters and var.domains allows any FQDN length, so a moderately long hostname plans cleanly and is rejected by the API at apply. Principle is a best fit (apply-time correctness).
findings.remediation: Truncate names over 63 characters to 54 and append an 8-character hash of the domain to keep them unique.
findings.title: Per-domain DNS authorization and map entry names can exceed the 63-character resource name limit
